issue.title: gcal: per-calendar row policy before syncing timed-event calendars like Time Blocks
issue.description:
## Feature proposal

Proposed by bob-cli-lr.5 (note #4), the enable-birthdays phase of epic bob-cli-lr
(plan:202611/gcal_calendar_marks.md). Filed by the bob-cli-lr land agent.

Every configured calendar uses the same row rules: timed events become Event Tasks
(checkbox, `#task`, MEET filing, root, ack), and all-day events become context rows.
That suits Birthdays (all-day only). A calendar of timed, non-meeting blocks such as
"Time Blocks" would flood the ledger with Event Tasks and MEET entries.

Define a per-calendar row policy before enabling such a calendar. For example, a
`gcal.calendars[N].rows: context | task` key (or ack/MEET opt-outs) that decides whether
that calendar's timed events become Event Tasks or context rows, and whether they file
under MEET or count as Pomodoro time. Document how a policy change migrates existing
rows under the three-way span merge.

## Why out of scope

bob-cli-lr listed "per-calendar ack or row-mode policy" as a v1 non-goal. It enabled
only Birthdays, whose all-day rows already classify as context rows.

## Evidence

- Plan § Non-goals (v1) and § Context ("All-day events already classify as context
  rows ... So no classifier change is needed").
- `src/native/gcal/classify.rs` decides Inclusion (Task vs Context) with no per-calendar
  input today.

task_type_fields.proposal: A per-calendar gcal.calendars policy key that decides whether that calendar's timed events become Event Tasks or context rows and whether they file under MEET or ack.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: bob-cli-lr made per-calendar ack and row-mode policy a v1 non-goal; Birthdays is all-day only.

issue.creation_reason: bob-cli-lr.5 proposed it as a planned follow-up; every synced calendar's timed events become Event Tasks, which would flood the ledger for block calendars.
